<p class="pg-lede">Source-specific hydrogen techno-economic parameters and inputs, preserving printed values, technical and monetary bases, source terms and paper cross-references. Includes historical status, design coefficients, targets, policy inputs, an observed retail price and a clearly labeled paper model assumption.</p>
<p class="ref-meta"><span class="chip">Version 0.1</span> <span class="chip">Checked 2026-11-13</span> <span class="chip">76 quantities</span></p>
<p class="ref-actions"><a href="hydrogen-v0.1.csv" class="btn-solid">Download versioned CSV</a> <a href="index.html#cite" class="btn-outline">How to cite</a></p>
<p>U.S. focus, with the global IRENA synthesis labeled separately. Coverage: 2007/2031. 2007 cost bases through the 2031 Hydrogen Shot goal, including historical status and 2026 policy and market inputs. Ultimate technology targets are undated.</p>
<p>Not a harmonized forecast: values keep their sources’ bases. NR means not reported; BOL means beginning of life; NOAK means nth-of-a-kind. Blank numeric CSV fields are missing values, never zero. Records with suffixes separate quantities or applicable years while keeping their common H-number. Costs have not been escalated.</p>
<p>“Paper use or numerical correspondence” distinguishes a stated model assumption from a matching number. A matching number alone does not establish adoption of a source or technology classification. All expanded basis and locator text is present in the page and the downloads.</p>

<section class="fx-sec" aria-labelledby="read-before-using">
<div class="fx-head"><h2 id="read-before-using">Read before using</h2></div>
<dl class="ref-risks">
<dt>Installed versus uninstalled</dt><dd>Equipment, installed direct cost, total installed capital (TIC), total overnight cost (TOC) and total capital investment (TCI) have different inclusions. Apply installation factors only after checking the boundary.</dd>
<dt>Stack versus system</dt><dd>Stack cost is part of system cost. Rectification and auxiliaries change electricity use; keep AC system input separate from DC stack ratings.</dd>
<dt>LHV versus HHV</dt><dd>Consumption in kWh/kg is a physical ratio; lower or higher heating value defines an efficiency percentage. Electrical-only SOEC efficiency retains an additional heat input.</dd>
<dt>Capacity versus output</dt><dd>Cost per kilogram stored, per kg/day of production capacity and per kilogram produced are different quantities.</dd>
<dt>Replacement versus O&amp;M</dt><dd>Check replacement timing and inclusions before combining annual maintenance with per-replacement fractions or replacement-inclusive O&amp;M.</dd>
<dt>Capture versus lifecycle</dt><dd>Process-carbon capture does not remove upstream methane, purchased-electricity or all combustion emissions. H52 is a reference-plant coefficient, not a lifecycle estimate.</dd>
<dt>Policy eligibility versus assumed support</dt><dd>A model’s support assumption does not establish statutory eligibility. Apply the production-year amount and the qualifying conditions together.</dd>
<dt>Production cost versus sale price</dt><dd>Hydrogen Shot is a production-cost goal. Retail prices include downstream services; neither is automatically a plant-gate sale price.</dd>
</dl>
</section>
<section class="fx-sec" aria-labelledby="disagreements">
<div class="fx-head"><h2 id="disagreements">Where sources disagree</h2></div>
<div class="ref-table-scroll" role="region" aria-label="Source disagreements" tabindex="0"><table class="ref-comparison" data-quarto-disable-processing="true"><caption>Source-version and definition differences</caption><thead><tr><th scope="col">Issue</th><th scope="col">Published values and sources</th><th scope="col">Interpretation</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><th scope="row">PEM stack lifetime</th><td>40,000 h (S1); 50,000–80,000 h (S5, Table 6, p. 65).<br><a href="#source-S1">S1</a> · <a href="#source-S5">S5</a></td><td>The 40,000–80,000 h envelope is not a confidence interval: endpoint definitions, technologies and duty cycles are not harmonized.</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Alkaline degradation</th><td>3.2 mV/kh (S2); 4.8 mV/kh (S4, Table A-2, p. 52).<br><a href="#source-S2">S2</a> · <a href="#source-S4">S4</a></td><td>The public documents disagree. Keep the document-specific values; do not average them or silently repair either source.</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Backup fuel-cell equipment cost</th><td>3,000 $/kW in the 2016 DOE PDF (S8); 6,100 $/kW in the later DOE webpage, both labeled 2015 status.<br><a href="#source-S8">S8</a> · <a href="https://www.energy.gov/cmei/fuels/doe-technical-targets-fuel-cell-backup-power-systems">Later DOE webpage</a></td><td>A source-version difference, not a validated market-price range. Preserve the version; cost years remain NR.</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>
</section>
<section class="fx-sec" aria-labelledby="gaps">
<div class="fx-head"><h2 id="gaps">Gaps</h2></div>
<p>Public-source coverage still needed for comparable inputs:</p><dl class="ref-risks">
<dt>ATR without CCS</dt><dd>The cited NETL report has no such case. Subtracting capture equipment from ATR+CCS does not supply a complete unabated design.</dd>
<dt>Unit-level CCS removal assumptions</dt><dd>NETL’s overall capture objective does not supply a universal solvent-removal input.</dd>
<dt>Before-capture intensity of capture-equipped plants</dt><dd>The unabated SMR coefficient H52 should not be transferred to SMR+CCS or ATR+CCS; their fuel and process balances differ.</dd>
<dt>Current PEM/alkaline variable O&amp;M</dt><dd>A comparable public benchmark excluding electricity, water and stack replacement is not established here. H27 is a model factor.</dd>
<dt>Current MW-scale, continuous-duty pure-hydrogen fuel cells</dt><dd>Installed CAPEX, variable O&amp;M and lifetime require suitable public sources. Backup-system values and natural-gas CHP efficiencies are unsuitable substitutes.</dd>
<dt>Current storage and pipeline procurement costs</dt><dd>Historical DOE component benchmarks need newer public estimates with installation and location stated.</dd>
<dt>Hydrogen-only U.S. wholesale prices</dt><dd>H65 is a small retail sample. The BLS/FRED argon-and-hydrogen series is a combined index, not a hydrogen-only price per kilogram. <a href="https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/WPU06790309">Public reference</a></dd>
<dt>Additional California retail coverage</dt><dd>The CEC/CARB assessment is a further public reference; its numerical observations are not included in this edition. <a href="https://www.energy.ca.gov/publications/2026/joint-agency-staff-report-assembly-bill-126-2025-annual-assessment-hydrogen">Public reference</a></dd>
</dl>
</section>

<section class="fx-sec" aria-labelledby="updates">
<div class="fx-head"><h2 id="updates">Update cadence</h2></div>
<p>This schedule describes planned source review; last checked 2026-11-13. Historical editions retain their original bases.</p><dl class="ref-risks">
<dt>45V statute and regulations</dt><dd>Monthly and after legislation, final rules or material guidance; recheck before each analysis.</dd>
<dt>45V monetary amounts</dt><dd>Annually when the IRS inflation notice appears; retain production-year applicability.</dd>
<dt>Electrolyzer and fuel-cell costs and targets</dt><dd>Six-month source check; annual handbook release; preserve historical editions.</dd>
<dt>Efficiency, lifetime, degradation and turndown</dt><dd>Annual review and whenever design or duty cycle changes.</dd>
<dt>Storage, pipelines and compression</dt><dd>Annual source review; update project-specific estimates before investment modeling.</dd>
<dt>Retail prices</dt><dd>Each quarterly DOE report; preserve sample, period and units.</dd>
<dt>Paper model assumptions</dt><dd>Retain the cited publication version.</dd>
</dl>
</section>
